entries.german:
Hartmann Groschlag v. Dieburg bittet Erzbischof Balduin (v. Luxemburg) von Trier, Verwalter des Stifts zu Mainz, um Zustimmung, dass er seine Ehefrau Grete, Tochter Eberhards v. Rosenberg, mit 250 Pfund Heller auf den genannten Lehen, die er, sein Bruder und ihre Ganerben von Mainz zu Dieburg innehaben, bewittumen kann, derart, dass nach seinem Tod seine nächsten Erben das Pfenniggeld oder Korngeld innerhalb von 14 Tagen vor St. Peterstag, der um Fastnacht liegt (22. Februar) und 14 Tage danach für die 250 Pfund lösen. Hartmann Ulner v. Dieburg, die Gebr. Johann und Oswald Groschlag v. Dieburg und ihre Ganerben bekunden ihre Zustimmung

Siegler: Hartmann, Johann und Oswald Groschlag v. Dieburg, Hartmann Ulner v. Dieburg
entries.english:
Hartmann Groschlag of Dieburg requests Archbishop Balduin (of Luxemburg) of Trier, administrator of the Mainz church, for his consent that he may endow his wife Grete, daughter of Eberhard von Rosenberg, with 250 pounds Heller on the aforementioned fiefs, which he, his brother, and their joint heirs hold from Mainz at Dieburg, such that after his death his nearest heirs may redeem the penny tax or grain tax within 14 days before St. Peter's Day, which falls around Shrove Tuesday (February 22), and 14 days thereafter for the 250 pounds. Hartmann Ulner of Dieburg, the brothers Johann and Oswald Groschlag of Dieburg and their joint heirs certify their consent.

Sealers: Hartmann, Johann and Oswald Groschlag of Dieburg, Hartmann Ulner of Dieburg.

facts.content: sought permission from Balduin of Trier to endow his wife Grete with a widow’s provision on the Mainz fiefs at Dieburg held by him, his brother, and their joint heirs.
